In mathematics, specifically in [[representation theory]], the '''Frobenius formula''', introduced by [[Ferdinand Georg Frobenius|G. Frobenius]], computes the [[character theory|characters]] of irreducible representations of the [[symmetric group]] ''S''<sub>''n''</sub>. Among the other applications, the formula can be used to derive the [[hook length formula]].

== Statement ==
Let <math>\chi_\lambda</math> be the [[character theory|character]] of an irreducible representation of the symmetric group <math>S_n</math> corresponding to a partition <math>\lambda</math> of ''n'': <math>n = \lambda_1 + \cdots + \lambda_k</math> and <math>\ell_j = \lambda_j + k - j</math>. For each partition <math>\mu</math> of ''n'', let <math>C(\mu)</math> denote the [[conjugacy class]] in <math>S_n</math> corresponding to it (cf. the example below), and let <math>i_j</math> denote the number of times ''j'' appears in <math>\mu</math> (so <math>\sum_j i_j j = n</math>). Then the '''Frobenius formula''' states that the constant value of <math>\chi_\lambda</math> on <math>C(\mu),</math>

:<math>\chi_\lambda(C(\mu)),</math>

is the coefficient of the monomial <math>x_1^{\ell_1} \dots x_k^{\ell_k}</math> in the homogeneous polynomial in <math>k</math> variables

: <math>\prod_{i < j}^k (x_i - x_j) \; \prod_j P_j(x_1, \dots, x_k)^{i_j},</math>

where <math>P_j(x_1, \dots, x_k) = x_1^j + \dots + x_k^j</math> is the <math>j</math>-th [[power sum]].

'''Example''': Take <math>n = 4</math>. Let <math>\lambda: 4 = 2 + 2 = \lambda_1 + \lambda_2</math> and hence <math>k=2</math>, <math>\ell_1=3</math>, <math>\ell_2=2</math>. If <math>\mu: 4 = 1 + 1 + 1 + 1</math> (<math>i_1=4</math>), which corresponds to the class of the identity element, then <math>\chi_\lambda(C(\mu))</math> is the coefficient of <math>x_1^3 x_2^2</math> in

:<math>(x_1 - x_2)P_1(x_1,x_2)^4=(x_1 - x_2)(x_1 + x_2)^4</math>

which is 2. Similarly, if <math>\mu: 4 = 3 + 1</math> (the class of a 3-cycle times an 1-cycle) and <math>i_1=i_3=1</math>, then <math>\chi_{\lambda}(C(\mu))</math>, given by

:<math>(x_1 - x_2)P_1(x_1,x_2)P_3(x_1,x_2)=(x_1 - x_2)(x_1 + x_2)(x_1^3 + x_2^3),</math>

is&nbsp;−1.

For the identity representation, <math>k=1</math> and <math>\lambda_1=n=\ell_1</math>. The character <math>\chi_\lambda(C(\mu))</math> will be equal to the coefficient of <math>x_1^n</math> in <math>\prod_j P_j(x_1)^{i_j}=\prod_j x_1^{i_j j}= x_1^{\sum_j i_j j}=x_1^n</math>, 
which is 1 for any <math>\mu</math> as expected.
